what: kb_search for schema-upgrade and SCHEMA_DIR did not surface the schema_dir setting. The GAPS entry R12-1 still says schema_dir is not in the kb. A later grep of the catalog found it in schema-evolution.agent.md line 27 only; build-process.md's schema-upgrade row (line 299) and its note (line 306) do not mention schema_dir.
why: The setting is documented only in the agent companion of schema-evolution; the build-process page that kb returns for schema-upgrade omits it.
workaround: Used schema_dir from the catalog grep; did not use schema-upgrade for the data-keeping migration.

what: Both actor types (Customer and Admin) are stored with anonymous=true. The builder's review says the catalog defines anonymous as a guest that is open to anyone, yet unauthenticated POSTs return 401 AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED, so the flag does not make the actor public at runtime as the catalog implies.
why: The catalog text (accesspoint rules) and the observed runtime behaviour disagree; the reviewer could not reconcile them from the catalog alone.
workaround: Recorded as review item R16-R3 and catalog item C3 in REVIEW-R16.md; no model change (review round).

what: The catalog contradicts itself on whether identifier flags are enforced: the composite-identifier practice says the agent-docs do not state how the flag is enforced, while structure.md line 75 says the runtime enforces it. The reviewer raised this as catalog item C4.
why: Two catalog pages describe the same flag with different claims.
workaround: Logged in REVIEW-R16.md as C4; webshop business keys (GiftCard.code, Invitation.inviteKey, Quote.number) were not flagged as identifiers (review R16-R11).

what: The catalog says application_hu-HU.json is generated from the model and must be listed in .generator-ignore. The webshop's make-hu-translations.py docstring says a new locale file is not a generated file and needs no ignore entry, and the file has survived 15 rounds of generation with no entry.
why: The generator only emits application_en-US.json for a one-language model; the Hungarian file is a hand-made locale, so the catalog text is wrong for this case.
workaround: Kept scripts/make-hu-translations.py as the source of the Hungarian file; no .generator-ignore entry.

what: The singleton page says whether and when the platform calls an initializer operation is not documented. The builder's seed for the ShopConfig row (R10-4) therefore has no documented startup hook.
why: The catalog does not describe a startup hook for initializers; the reference-data page also leaves it open.
workaround: scripts/seed-dev-user.sh and a manual seed; ShopConfig seed still open.

what: The interceptor page says getInstance() identifies the instance with its old values, while getInput() carries the new values. The builder's audit interceptor re-reads the old row through the DAO, so the page does not say whether the instance payload is reliable for old values.
why: The one-line description is ambiguous about which fields the instance payload holds.
workaround: ProductAuditInterceptor reads the old product through productDao.getById before compare.

what: The Quartz page says the platform provides no scheduler and that the docs do not describe the transaction or variable context of a plain scheduler thread. The builder needs that context for the F73 release job.
why: The catalog gives no transaction or ACTOR variable model for threads outside a request.
workaround: Planned to manage UserTransaction inside each job, per the Quartz practice; F73 not built in this round.

what: Review item C9: the injectable-clock recipe in the catalog says LocalDateTime.now follows the JVM time zone and Timestamp!now follows defaultZoneId, but the builder's review says the recipe uses systemDefaultZone, which clashes with the platform zone.
why: The clock recipe mixes two zone sources; the review cites a clash the catalog text does not state in this chunk.
workaround: Recorded as catalog item C9 in REVIEW-R16.md; not re-verified against the recipe code in this chunk.

what: Builder reports that agent-docs/backend/interceptors.agent.md still says getInstance() identifies the instance as 'old values', which contradicts the full interceptors page (N1 in the re-check).
why: Builder's reading of the condensed companion page versus the full page; the chunk shows only snippets, so the contradiction is not confirmed here.

what: agent-docs/backend/platform-behavior-reference.md says the platform has no scheduler and no Quartz component. best-practices/backend/quartz-scheduled-job.md describes starting Quartz through a scheduler activator. The two pages disagree.
why: The Quartz practice describes a Karaf scheduler setup that the platform page says does not exist in the runtime.
workaround: Built an OSGi component with its own executor instead (ReservationJob).

what: The docs do not say what transaction and variable context a plain scheduler thread has. The builder wrote its own transaction handling and cannot use ACTOR in the job.
why: Scheduler threads are outside the request context; the catalog says so only in general terms.
workaround: Job calls a modeled static operation through the dispatcher; no ACTOR is used.

what: Dispatcher.callOperation takes the operation name in the form <asm package>.<Entity>#<operation>. The catalog does not give this form; the builder found it in webshop-asm.model.
why: The catalog shows only the interceptor FQN form, not the callOperation name.
workaround: Used webshop.ShopJobs#releaseExpired taken from the generated ASM model.

what: kb says the checksum file is .generated-files__[actor_fqn] in the module root. The real files in the frontend modules are .generated-files-customer and .generated-files-admin, plus an empty .generated-files.
why: Catalog naming does not match the generated layout.
workaround: Read the real file names with ls before comparing checksums.

what: kb suggests 'mvn clean install -Dignore-checksums' for formatting-only checksum errors. judo.sh build -i sets -DvalidateChecksum=false (judo.sh about line 819). The builder used the judo.sh property; the kb flag was not checked.
why: The catalog flag name does not match what judo.sh passes.
workaround: Ran mvnd with -DvalidateChecksum=false (build still failed for other reasons).

what: A build without -i fails on every generated frontend file ('There are manual changes in the generated files', listing all of src/ in both actors). The build itself reformats generated code with biome after writing, so checksums never match again.
why: build -i leaves the frontend .generated-files empty, and the post-generation format step changes the files; the catalog presents -i only as an option for formatting-only changes.
workaround: Use ./judo.sh build -i for every build from here on.
proposed_target: agent-docs/frontend/README.md (Build fails with checksum mismatch error)

what: agent-docs/deployment/local-development.md says build -a updates custom operations for a running backend. In this layout build -a and build -F -KA update ~/.m2 but not application/.karaf/system, which is what ./judo.sh start runs. The app then lacked the new custom operations and interceptor.
why: Start uses the copies in .karaf/system; only a full build refreshes them. Evidence: system jar dated 14:30 without the new classes, m2 jar 14:45 with them.
workaround: Full ./judo.sh build -i before start; the debug interceptor and later fixes were only picked up after that.

what: A static operation on an unmapped transfer object cannot be reached by an access: validate fails with 'Access target have to be mapped'. operation.md ends the unmapped section with 'Verify: how an actor reaches the operation was not settled in source'.
why: The catalog leaves the access route open; the validator rule is the only evidence.
workaround: Mapped the transfer object to the one ShopConfig row (no members) and put the static operation on it.

what: best-practices/frontend/dual-actor-frontend-architecture.md says the pattern extends to three or more actors, including an anonymous public actor. In this model a third actor (anonymous SYSTEM) breaks the admin frontend build.
why: The catalog claim is not true for this generator version (see c12-15).
workaround: Removed the third actor from the model.

what: Kb says 'set just those fields on an entity that was not loaded in full' but does not say how to build a payload with identifier and version in custom code.
why: The Pattern 4 text gives the mask and entity idea but not the payload construction.
workaround: Read the generated Product.from and used ProductBuilder.from(Map.of(__identifier, __entityType, __version, stock, soldUnits)).

what: Plain build without -i fails on every generated frontend file because the frontend build itself reformats generated code; the REVIEW-R16 advice to build without -i was wrong, and build -i leaves the checksum file empty.
why: Build reformats generated files, so a later generate reports manual changes; the catalog does not state that -i is required for the round cycle.
workaround: Always run ./judo.sh build -f -i (and generate -i) in the round scripts.

what: No catalog recipe for a partial update with optimistic locking: the mask only shapes the read-back, the write still needs the version in the payload, and a stale version must be re-read and retried.
why: data-access-guide Pattern 4 (Partial Updates) does not say that the mask does not limit the write nor how to combine it with __version.
workaround: StockService writes only identifier, version, stock and soldUnits, re-reads on stale version, and returns NOT_ENOUGH_STOCK when stock is gone.

what: custom-post-detail-views says a custom view replaces the default container layout, but the mechanism is one custom implementation element per field of the view; the whole view cannot be replaced, so every field needs a model mark and a register call.
why: Catalog describes a whole-view replacement that the platform does not offer; the implementation pattern in the blueprint is the per-element route.
workaround: Marked all fields of the detail views as custom implementation; first element renders the whole summary layout, others render nothing.

what: Builder found that the graphql view shows representationComponent null for TransferObjectTable (for example ShopProductInfo Product_Table) while relation TabularReferenceFields carry table; setting representationComponent=card on a TransferObjectTable with update works.
why: Attribute is documented on TransferObjectTable in ui.md, but the query did not show it, so the builder relied on the update result.
workaround: Used update ... --set representationComponent=card and checked with status.

what: Pointing the Vite dev server at the Karaf backend needs VITE_API_DEFAULT_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8181; the app uses hash routes (#/Customer/...), so direct path URLs do not open the screen. The builder found both by reading main.tsx, after the kb guard fired.
why: Dev-server setup for HMR is not in the catalog path the builder read (development-workflow).
workaround: Started npx vite with VITE_API_DEFAULT_BASE_URL set and added playwright.dev.config.ts (local override) to target it.
proposed_target: catalog/agent-docs/frontend/development-workflow.md (Vite dev server against a Karaf backend)

what: The top bar clipped the navigation ('MY ACCOU'). The builder tuned spaceRequired (4, then 3, then 2), search width, avatar name and gaps through several iterations to fit the nav at 1280 and 1440 px.
why: spaceRequired moves grid columns only; the catalog says nothing about sizing the extra component against the generated horizontal nav width.
workaround: Iterated CSS and spaceRequired in AppBarExtras.tsx and application-customizer.tsx; at 1280 px the last nav group sits behind the scroll arrow (R16U-6).

what: The wishlist items list cannot show a price through the shared Price component: the column customizer hook is never applied and a custom column does not compile, so the wishlist is a custom component over the generated service.
why: Builder claim recorded in code comment (GAPS R12); not checked in this chunk.
workaround: WishlistItems custom element with name, price and two actions.
proposed_target: column customizer hook on the generated table

what: Opening a notification marks it read through postRefreshAction calling markRead; the code comment says a write in a backend interceptor on the read was not kept.
why: Builder observation recorded in a code comment; no evidence in the chunk beyond the comment.
workaround: Client-side markRead in registerNotificationHook.ts.

what: The cards container shows no table operations, loading state or empty state; the hook has to add the action bar, loading and empty states itself.
why: The catalog describes the cards hook as a table replacement but does not list what the table adds.
workaround: Hook adds toolbar, action bar and empty state; shared ListBars.tsx.

what: best-practices/backend/email-service-integration.md says the agent-docs do not describe the EmailService API. agent-docs/backend/platform-behavior-reference.agent.md has an 'Email Service' section with sendMessage(EmailMessage.emailBuilder()), the fields, attachments, inline content and the IllegalArgumentException for an invalid address.
why: The practice page was written before the agent-doc section existed or was not updated.
workaround: Used the agent-doc section (as found by the builder via javap).

what: Compile against the platform e-mail API needs osgi-email-api as a provided dependency; the builder added it to generator-overrides/app/pom.xml.extra-dependencies.fragment.hbs and to the order-tests pom, the same way F39 added handlebars.
why: The e-mail API bundle is in the Karaf runtime and not in the generated app pom; the catalog does not say how to compile against it.
workaround: Provided-scope dependency in the generator-overrides fragment and order-tests pom.

what: Mail rows failed with 'The platform mail service is not available.' after switching to SMTP localhost:1025 (log SMTP server off). Karaf log showed the osgi-email bundles started; JavaMailSenderActivator is configuration-policy=require. The builder added SMTP user and password and restarted; the root cause was not confirmed in the chunk.
why: Unknown. kb says the mail service (JavaMailSenderActivator) is created only when the log SMTP server is off; the builder checked the config templates.
workaround: Added JUDO_PLATFORM_MAIL_SMTP_USER and PASSWORD to judo-karaf.env and restarted; F77 spec still open at chunk end.

what: The builder says the app bundle has no JSON library, so it wrote a small MiniJson reader for the flat array of objects. The Karaf feature list it printed includes jackson-features.
why: Unverified claim; the bulk JSON practice does not say which library the runtime provides.
workaround: Custom MiniJson.java reader (about 100 lines).

what: After a build with -a, the running app still ran the previous code: start unpacks the karaf-offline tarball, which kept the old app jar, so the mail retry change was not visible in the tests.
why: build -a only refreshes the jar in ~/.m2; start uses the offline tarball. The catalog calls -a 'fast Java iteration' without this limit.
workaround: Ran full ./judo.sh build -i -M -F, then restarted and reran the spec.

what: Setting JUDO_PLATFORM_MAIL_SMTP_HOST and PORT in judo-karaf.env is not enough to get an EmailService OSGi service; the catalog deployment section does not say what else is needed.
why: Deployment doc incomplete for the mail service; the app started but the EmailService reference was null.
workaround: Shop sends mail through its own path; no EmailService used in this round.

what: The doc says the log SMTP server listens on logSmtpServerPort, default 1025; the shipped template says 10025.
why: Catalog default port does not match the shipped template.
workaround: Read only; log SMTP server was off.

what: The handlebars email template example compiles the template itself and passes it as htmlTemplate; the platform renders htmlTemplate again, so copying the example renders twice.
why: Example conflicts with the Email Service reference (htmlTemplate and plaintTemplate are Handlebars templates applied to model).
workaround: Shop renders subject and body itself, once.
catalog_paths: catalog/best-practices (handlebars-email-template.md, path not confirmed in session)

what: The catalog says check the artifact for the platform mail API but gives no coordinates; the working artifact is hu.blackbelt:osgi-email-api, compile-only.
why: Email integration doc has no dependency coordinates.
workaround: Added compile-only dependency in generator-overrides app pom fragment.
catalog_paths: catalog/agent-docs (email-service-integration, platform-email-template-service; exact paths not confirmed in session)

what: An additive migration gives an existing singleton ShopConfig row the new column defaults for some attributes but not for others (mailFrom empty); the code falls back to defaults on empty values.
why: Schema-evolution doc says an additive change needs no manual step; it does not say existing rows may keep empty values.
workaround: Code treats empty values as defaults.

what: Import of a CSV or JSON file threw NullPointerException on .isPresent(): an unsent optional transient binary input is null, not Optional.empty().
why: Catalog does not say optional operation members can be null.
workaround: StartImportCustomImplementation checks x != null && x.isPresent().

what: No documented way to declare a database index on a model attribute; the agent-docs list indexes only among RDBMS settings.
why: Catalog gap for indexes needed for 50 000 rows.
workaround: Checked the database for existing indexes with psql.

what: With -DuseCache=true the frontend-react model step fails with an empty cause '{}: {}'; -DuseCache=false and -DvalidateModels=false give exit 0.
why: Build cache hides the real validation error in quick mode.
workaround: Ran mvnd install with -DuseCache=false -DvalidateModels=true to see the error.

what: After a model change the new table did not exist: relation t_webshop_product_version does not exist; the schema upgrade is not run by judo.sh start.
why: Schema upgrade is a separate step before start.
workaround: Ran schema upgrade before start (per GAPS R18-12).

what: Zeta transformation YAML option (the orchestrator asked to use YAML where the build supports it for Zeta) is not documented in the catalog; the builder did not log this as a GAP in the visible GAPS writes.
why: kb search and grep of model-validation-and-transformation.md show only ETL vs ZETA and the judo.transformation.mode setting; no YAML mention.
workaround: Zeta used with the default settings (build log shows Zeta ESM to PSM, PSM to ASM).

what: Catalog has no Markdown to PDF recipe; builder wrote its own small renderer (MarkdownPdf on PDFBox) and reuses it for the report PDF.
why: Catalog covers Handlebars templates and the legacy DOCX XDocReport pipeline only.
workaround: MarkdownPdf (F39) reused.

what: Fresh PostgreSQL container (default max_connections 100) ran out of connections: sorry, too many clients already, once the app and Keycloak started.
why: The application keeps several connection pools; the catalog has no sizing advice for max_connections.
workaround: max_connections=300 in the compose database command.

what: After a new actor was added, generate did not add its module to frontend-react/pom.xml, e2e/pom.xml, karaf-features pom.xml and feature.xml; build -f did not pick it up. Builder copied those four files from the guest-actor branch.
why: Probable: module registration happens only in a full build or a generate-root step; not confirmed.
workaround: git checkout of the four files from branch guest-actor, then full build -i.

what: Keycloak user customer/customer had to be created by hand through the admin REST API because there was no recipe for a first login user in the minimal app.
why: Known gap (GAPS item 8 from an earlier round); catalog recipe for seeding a first user not found in this chunk.
workaround: Created the user through the admin REST API and tested the token.

what: accesspoint.md marks access control for a call with no principal as 'Verify' (not checked). The builder did not check it either; it only confirmed that the call works with no token.
why: Catalog does not state whether an anonymous call can read more than the intended product fields.

what: ./judo.sh generate overwrote the Guest application-customizer.tsx with the default stub ('register your implementations here'). The builder restored its own copy from /tmp and rewrote it.
why: The generator rewrites a new actor's customizer when generated files around it change (builder's note in GAPS R19-18). Confirmed by .generated-files-guest, which lists the file.
workaround: Copy saved to /tmp/guestcustom before generate and restored after; the file was written again and build -i checked with grep CatalogHome.
